ops.body: StringsTemplate writes an Oxygen Not Included mod's translation template and checks its translations from the built mod DLL, without launching the game. It is a .NET 8 console app (C# 9) that loads the DLL against the game's own assemblies in the `Managed` folder, runs the `ModStrings` initializers and walks that class tree the way `Isochronous.Translations` (`common/src/Translations.cs`) registers it: `ModStrings.A.B.C` is the key `STRINGS.A.B.C`, with the field's English text. Run as `StringsTemplate <game Managed dir> <mod dll> <translations dir>`, it rewrites `<Mod>.pot` in the translations folder, reports missing, stale, empty, obsolete and refused entries in every `<locale>.po` there, checks that every PLib `[Option]` key written as a `STRINGS.` key exists, and exits 1 on a `FAIL` (no `ModStrings` class, no `LocString` fields, an unknown option key, a po that does not parse) or when a po has missing, stale or refused entries, and 2 for a usage error. The mod developer runs it through `tools/Translations/translations.py` after changing strings and before a release; that script builds this tool and runs it for every mod whose csproj sets `<UseTranslations>true</UseTranslations>`.
